data.title: For 75 San Joaquin County Families, Affordable Housing May be Within Reach thanks to Health Net
data.description:
The company's $3 million investment will help create 75 affordable homes for income-qualified Stockton families.

STOCKTON, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Health Net, one of California's most experienced Medi-Cal managed care health plans and company of Centene Corporation (), today announced a $3 million investment in the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund. The funding will provide grants and low-interest loans to accelerate affordable housing developments and support the creation of at least 75 affordable homes for Stockton families facing some of the region's most significant housing challenges.

"A home is so much more than a roof overhead. It's the place where families feel safe, children can grow and learn, and people can focus on their health and well-being," said Dorothy M. Seleski, Medi-Cal Plan President at Health Net. "Too many families in our communities are struggling to find housing they can afford. By partnering with the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund, we're helping create more opportunities for families to put down roots, build stability and look toward the future with greater confidence. Together, we're investing in healthier communities by helping more people find a place to call home."

The investment will support community-driven housing developments, with a focus on serving families facing the greatest barriers to affordable housing, including households earning between 30% and 50% of the area median income.

"When local organizations unite around a shared goal, communities move forward," said San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund Board Chair Gary Singh. "Health Net's investment will help transform plans into homes for local families while encouraging broader community participation in addressing the region's housing needs."

The investment will support eligible projects through January 2029, from planning through construction.

"Investments in affordable housing are investments in the health, strength and future of our communities," said San Joaquin County Supervisor Robert Rickman. "By bringing public, private and community partners together, we can help more San Joaquin County families find stable housing and create lasting opportunity across the region."

In Sacramento and San Joaquin counties, Health Net has invested a combined $11 million in affordable housing and related initiatives, including $2 million to Stanislaus Equity Partners, Inc. (STEP) and $3 million to Fairview Terrace. By supporting developments at every stage, from planning and financing to construction and occupancy, Health Net is helping expand access to affordable housing, strengthen local communities and create the conditions for better health across the region.

About Health Net

Founded in California more than 45 years ago, Health Net, LLC ("Health Net"), a company of Centene Corporation, believes that every person deserves a safety net for their health, regardless of age, income, employment status or current state of health. Today, we provide health plans for individuals, families, businesses of every size and people who qualify for Medi-Cal or Medicare. With more than 117,000 of our network providers, Health Net serves more than three million members across the state. We also offer access to substance abuse programs, behavioral health services and managed healthcare products related to prescription drugs. We make these health plans and services available through Health Net and its subsidiaries: Health Net of California, Inc., Health Net Life Insurance Company and Health Net Community Solutions, Inc. These entities are wholly owned subsidiaries of Centene Corporation (), a leading healthcare enterprise committed to transforming the health of the communities we serve, one person at a time. Health Net and Centene Corporation employ more than 5,700 people in California who work at one of five regional Talent Hub offices. For more information, visit www.HealthNet.com.

data.title: US extends shipping law waiver 90 days, to allow freer movement of oil, commodities
data.description:
President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Reuters reported on Thursday that industry sources said the administration would extend the waiver on the more than 100-year-old Jones Act.

It has been the longest waiver in the history of the shipping law.

The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched the war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. In August, it extended the waiver but mandated that decisions would be made on a case-by-case basis, a stipulation continued through the latest waiver.

The ⁠Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies and crewed by American workers. Allowing the waiver aims to lower gas, diesel and fertilizer prices driven up by the war on Iran by increasing shipping flexibility and reducing transport bottlenecks.

The length of waivers has been limited in the past as the Jones Act is supported by the domestic shipbuilding business, a powerful lobby across the country.

data.title: Virgin Galactic Touches 52-Week Low After Update on Financing, Commercial Operations
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Shares of Virgin Galactic hit a 52-week low after the company discussed plans for its financing and commercial operations and reported quarterly results.

The stock down 27%, to $1.96, midday Friday after touching an intraday low of $1.95. It has fallen about 39% this year.

Virgin Galactic said it expects to increase capacity to 150 spaceflights a year by the end of 2028. The company began booking a limited tranche of Spaceflight Expeditions at $850,000 a seat.

In October, the company said it expected commercial spaceflights to start in the second quarter of 2027. It previously delayed the target to February 2027 from the fourth quarter of 2026.

In a securities filing Thursday, Virgin Galactic said it intended to exchange stock for 2.5% convertible senior notes due 2027 and that it entered an open market sale agreement for the potential sale of up to $250 million of stock "as part of a comprehensive plan to support its operations and growth initiatives."

On Friday, the company said in a filing it entered an agreement with a noteholder for a $12.5 million exchange.

Third-quarter revenue was $427,000, up from $365,000 a year earlier, the company reported Thursday afternoon. Loss was 39 cents a share, compared with a loss of $1.09 a share a year earlier.

Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com

data.title: CFTC’s Selig accuses states of trying to ‘lock up’ prediction market founders
data.description:
Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig is turning up the heat on his criticisms of states' handling of lawsuits brought against prediction market platforms and their executives.

Speaking at the Cantor Convergence conference, Selig called the state suits "really egregious" and defended the platforms operating under what he has long called the CFTC's "exclusive jurisdiction."

"We're seeing states bring criminal charges, essentially trying to lock up founders and CEOs of these companies that are offering lawful products under a federal regime," he said.

The comments come amid a stretch of battles between the CFTC and roughly a dozen states and cities over whether event contracts offered on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket constitute illegal gambling. Selig argued that the disagreements should be hashed out in court without threatening executives with time in prison.

"Somebody says it's gambling, somebody says it's a derivative," he said. "That's not something that should be at the risk of going to jail."

And instead of fighting on a case-by-case basis in multiple states, Selig wants to see the issue raised to the Supreme Court in a bid to solidify the CFTC's authority.

"I don't understand whether we're going to have every major CEO of an exchange locked up in a jail cell in Utah, or if we can just go to the Supreme Court and hash this thing out on the merits," he said.

On Thursday, the Justice Department and CFTC sued Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin to block his action against Kalshi.

Louisiana also filed a lawsuit Thursday targeting companies including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase.

"I am concerned that some of the states are getting very aggressive," Selig said. "We’ll continue to defend our jurisdiction."

data.title: Wendy's emerges as stalking horse bidder for franchisee assets
data.description:
Wendy’s is offering $46M for 163 fast food restaurants owned by bankrupt franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group, one of Wendy’s largest franchisees and the recent plaintiff in a lawsuit against the restaurant chain.

Divine Infinity Operations has offered $18.6M for 42 of Meritage’s Wendy’s restaurants.

Meritage, which declared bankruptcy in September, sued Wendy’s over the termination of several hundred of its franchise agreements, an action Wendy’s took over unpaid royalties and fees. A day after the termination, Meritage filed for bankruptcy to prevent Wendy’s from taking over its 300+ restaurants.

Wendy’s terminated Meritage’s franchisee agreements due to unpaid royalties and fees. At the same time, Meritage blamed its restaurants' poor performance on Wendy’s ineffective marketing and promotional strategies.

As part of Wendy’s offer, it would forgive the $147M in fee and royalty payments from Meritage, pay an additional $6M for four real estate parcels in Ohio and Michigan, and reinstate franchise agreements that were canceled to allow for the transaction to occur.

According to Bloomberg, the deal also allows for separate sale processes for restaurant groups in Connecticut, Massachusetts, North Carolina, and Tennessee, and the closure of underperforming restaurants.

The stalking horse bid for Meritage’s assets was filed on Thursday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Michigan.

data.title: SEC plans to amend employee compensation disclosure rules
data.description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is proposing amendments to its employee compensation disclosure rules.

The regulator has proposed reducing the number of named executive officers to encompass the principal executive officer and principal financial officer, the positions whose compensation are generally most material for investors due to their roles in managing the company's most consequential matters.

The revision brings down the number from typically five or more individuals under the current rule to two in most circumstances.

Additionally, the SEC proposed modifying the primary executive compensation tabular disclosure requirements into three new tables from four to streamline and clarify the presentation. The three new tables will have information on earned compensation, granted compensation, and status of equity awards.

Also, the SEC proposed raising its minimum aggregate reporting threshold for perquisites from $10,000 to $150,000, revising interpretive guidance regarding perquisites, and simplifying the pay-versus-performance disclosure requirement, among other changes.

"Today, the Commission proposed amendments to its executive compensation disclosure requirements contained in Item 402 of Regulation S-K," said SEC Chairman Paul Atkins.

The proposed changes are expected to make the regulator's executive and director compensation disclosure requirements more principles-based and materiality-driven.

The proposal comes amid Atkins' efforts to reduce friction for companies looking to join and remain in public markets. Mega IPOs have made headlines recently, including SpaceX and SK Hynix , among others; with several others set to debut, including Anthropic , OpenAI , etc.

data.title: Gold Ticks Higher As Concerns Of Stagflation Emerge Amid Ongoing U.S.-Iran Faceoff
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After three sessions of losses, gold prices have ticked higher on Friday as the current U.S.-Iran standoff fuels concerns of possible rate hikes by U.S. Federal Reserve as well as stagflation in the economy if oil prices continue to surge.

Front Month Comex Gold for December delivery has edged up by $3.70 (or 0.10%) to $3,889.00 per troy ounce.

Meanwhile, front Month Comex Silver for December delivery has tumbled by $0.945 (or 1.89%) to $49.120 per troy ounce.

Since yesterday, investors have wound up their expectations on both a U.S.-Iran deal as well as the early reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

After Iranian leaders expressed strong remarks against the U.S., U.S. President Donald Trump messaged through Truth Social that the U.S. is no longer interested in any deal with Iran.

Following the Republican party's defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, Trump did not announce his plans on Iran until Saturday.

On Sunday, Trump stated that a renewal of attacks on Iran would be highly unlikely.

Later on Wednesday, remarking that he was seeing positive momentum in negotiations, Trump decided to pause the strikes on Iran at the request of Arabian leaders even though he continued to enforce the economic and naval blockade. Speaking in a similar vein, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio asserted that no combat actions were needed against Iran.

Sounding contrastingly different, the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei denied any negotiations with the U.S.

Reviving optimism, the Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. Vice President JD Vance will meet the Iranian hardliners face to face for negotiations.

Yesterday, trouncing all speculation, Trump messaged through Truth Social that the days when the U.S. waited for an agreement with Iran are over and he currently does not want any deal.

Following an U.S. airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik yesterday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced destroying a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain.

Contradicting this claim, U.S. Central Command announced shooting down two Iranian drones launched towards Bahrain.

Though rising oil prices could push inflation higher, experts are of the view that a prolonged delay in U.S.-Iran truce could lead to demand destruction in the economy, which could lead to stagflation.

On the economic front, data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics revealed that on a month-on-month basis in October, producer prices (considered a proxy for wholesale prices) increased 0.3%, easing sharply from an upwardly revised 1.4% increase in September and coming in below market expectations of 0.4%, largely reflecting moderating energy price pressures.

On an annual basis, the PPI increased by 6.50% from the previous year in October, the most since November of 2022.

The core producer prices (which exclude food and energy goods) increased by 0.3%, in line with market forecasts. On a yearly basis, the prices held at 5% for a second month in October, matching expectations.

Though the monthly data showed a slowdown, the annual numbers are higher than last year.

Analysts assessed the input against the recent Consumer Price Index readings and the core CPI, both of which came above market forecasts.

In the U.S. stock markets, optimism on technology shares showed a gradual comeback.

Over the past few days, the news about the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kept pressure on the company's stock. Following his resignation yesterday, the shares tumbled by more than 4%.

In an interview with CNBC, acknowledging that inflation is beginning to spread and proving far more persistent than analysts expected, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee stated that the U.S. Federal Reserve has got work to do on inflation.

Today, the U.S. dollar index was last seen trading at 103.34, up by 0.17 (or 0.16%) today.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, investors are currently betting on a 89.4% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike at the upcoming meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on December 8-,9 while the odds on rates being raised by 50 basis points stand at 10.6%.
